trust_decision.summary: How deep input nesting may drive the recursive write_all_values/write_one_value copy before failing with IERR_STACK_OVERFLOW; decided by one compile-time ceiling ION_MAX_RECURSION_DEPTH checked against preader->_depth in _ion_writer_write_all_values_helper. The fix only lowers that constant from 5000 to DEFAULT_MAX_CONTAINER_DEPTH (1000) so it fits a 1MB Windows stack.

landing_point.why: The only use of ION_MAX_RECURSION_DEPTH, and the only recursive reader-driven consumer in the library. A grep for the constant or 'recurs' finds it at once.

fix_sites.entry_point: ion_writer_write_all_values (public API, ionc/include/ionc/ion_writer.h:275), consumed at ionc/ion_writer.c:2722 -> 2744; also reached recursively from _ion_writer_write_one_value_helper at ionc/ion_writer.c:2689

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No O2 site or O8 route exists. The other recursive consumers already carry their own smaller limits (scanner skip 512, CLI event stream 100, extractor bounded by path length), so there is nothing to dismiss.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate nesting up to the default max_container_depth (1000) must still round-trip through ion_writer_write_all_values. A ceiling set below 1000, or a check against the user's max_container_depth instead of a fixed ceiling, would break default-configured deep documents or the existing option semantics.

O6_input_shapes: deeply nested text lists/sexps/structs fed through write_all_values (e.g. '[' * N)
binary-encoded nesting through the same helper (reader type does not matter, check is on preader->_depth)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The text scanner's recursive _ion_scanner_skip_container uses its own ION_SCANNER_MAX_SKIP_DEPTH (ionc/ion_scanner.h:442) and not ION_MAX_RECURSION_DEPTH. A copy where that limit is raised or tied to the reader option would be a separate recursion route.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer raising the skip limit so it allows max_container_depth-deep skipping (the test at test/test_ion_overflow.cpp:486-490 already raises max_container_depth above the skip depth) is a natural change. It is still a where-type sibling.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: _ion_extractor_match_helper recurses once per container. Today it is bounded only by active paths (fixed path length). A wildcard/descendant-path feature would make it unbounded by input.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Recursive descent is the existing style, and a 'match at any depth' option is a plausible feature addition.

O9_family: CWE-674 uncontrolled recursion / stack exhaustion (limit tuning)

O10_build.toolchain: CMake + C99 compiler; GoogleTest for test/
O10_build.project_tests: test/test_ion_overflow.cpp IonContainerDepth suite (e.g. WriteAllValuesDoesNotExhaustTheStack at test/test_ion_overflow.cpp:621-649, which already asserts IERR_STACK_OVERFLOW at 60000 levels). Reproducing the actual bug needs a small stack (1MB, debug frames), e.g. running the copy in a thread with a reduced stack size.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Bound the recursion by the user's max_container_depth, or convert the helper to iteration, instead of lowering the fixed ceiling to fit a 1MB stack.

out_of_scope_notes: tools/events/ion_event_stream.cpp:444-453 CLI event-stream recursion has its own ceiling of 100 (tools/events/ion_event_util.h:22); it is bounded and not part of the library fix.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell sizing). tiny_repo is inferred from 26 C sources in ionc/ plus decNumber, with no ion-tests submodule checked out.
Did not exhaustively audit ion_reader_text.c / ion_reader_binary.c step-out or skip paths for recursion. The grep for 'recurs' and skip helpers found only the scanner skip (bounded at 512).
Whether 1000 debug-build frames actually fit 1MB on Windows was not checked. The fix's own comment is the only evidence (fix.diff:16-19).
j_defence_ineffective=1 because the 5000 ceiling existed but was too high for small stacks; this rests on the fix's comment, not on a measurement.
